verses.text: These are the words of the Teacher, the son of David, king in Jerusalem:

xrefs.text: “Futility of futilities,” says the Teacher. “Everything is futile!”
I, the Teacher, was king over Israel in Jerusalem.
“Behold,” says the Teacher, “I have discovered this by adding one thing to another to find an explanation.
Thus the time that Solomon reigned in Jerusalem over all Israel was forty years.
but Rehoboam still reigned over the Israelites living in the cities of Judah.

verses.text: “Futility of futilities,” says the Teacher, “futility of futilities! Everything is futile!”

xrefs.text: Man is like a breath; his days are like a passing shadow.
For the creation was subjected to futility, not by its own will, but because of the One who subjected it, in hope
He who loves money is never satisfied by money, and he who loves wealth is never satisfied by income. This too is futile.
You, indeed, have made my days as handbreadths, and my lifetime as nothing before You. Truly each man at his best exists as but a breath. Selah
“Futility of futilities,” says the Teacher. “Everything is futile!”

verses.text: What does a man gain from all his labor, at which he toils under the sun?

xrefs.text: What does the worker gain from his toil?
For what does a man get for all the toil and striving with which he labors under the sun?
This too is a grievous affliction: Exactly as a man is born, so he will depart. What does he gain as he toils for the wind?

Yet when I considered all the works that my hands had accomplished and what I had toiled to achieve, I found everything to be futile, a pursuit of the wind; there was nothing to be gained under the sun.
What does it profit a man to gain the whole world, yet forfeit his soul?

verses.text: Generations come and generations go, but the earth remains forever.

xrefs.text: He set the earth on its foundations, never to be moved.
Where are your fathers now? And the prophets, do they live forever?
For who knows what is good for a man during the few days in which he passes through his fleeting life like a shadow? Who can tell a man what will come after him under the sun?
Heaven and earth will pass away, but My words will never pass away.
Your faithfulness continues through all generations; You established the earth, and it endures.

verses.text: The sun rises and the sun sets; it hurries back to where it rises.

xrefs.text: For the choirmaster. A Maskil of the sons of Korah. As the deer pants for streams of water, so my soul longs after You, O God.
their voice has gone out into all the earth, their words to the ends of the world. In the heavens He has pitched a tent for the sun.
Sun and moon stood still in their places at the flash of Your flying arrows, at the brightness of Your shining spear.
his offspring shall endure forever, and his throne before Me like the sun,
As long as the earth endures, seedtime and harvest, cold and heat, summer and winter, day and night shall never cease.”

verses.text: The wind blows southward, then turns northward; round and round it swirls, ever returning on its course.

xrefs.text: The wind blows where it wishes. You hear its sound, but you do not know where it comes from or where it is going. So it is with everyone born of the Spirit.
As you do not know the path of the wind, or how the bones are formed in a mother’s womb, so you cannot understand the work of God, the Maker of all things.
He calmed the storm to a whisper, and the waves of the sea were hushed.
The tempest comes from its chamber, and the cold from the driving north winds.
You whose clothes get hot when the land lies hushed under the south wind,

verses.text: All the rivers flow into the sea, yet the sea is never full; to the place from which the streams come, there again they flow.

xrefs.text: when I fixed its boundaries and set in place its bars and doors,

verses.text: All things are wearisome, more than one can describe; the eye is not satisfied with seeing, nor the ear content with hearing.

xrefs.text: Sheol and Abaddon are never satisfied; so the eyes of man are never satisfied.
Come to Me, all you who are weary and burdened, and I will give you rest.

There is a man all alone, without even a son or brother. And though there is no end to his labor, his eyes are still not content with his wealth: “For whom do I toil and bereave my soul of enjoyment?” This too is futile— a miserable task.

To the man who is pleasing in His sight, He gives wisdom and knowledge and joy, but to the sinner He assigns the task of gathering and accumulating that which he will hand over to one who pleases God. This too is futile and a pursuit of the wind.
Blessed are those who hunger and thirst for righteousness, for they will be filled.

verses.text: What has been will be again, and what has been done will be done again; there is nothing new under the sun.

xrefs.text: What exists has already been, and what will be has already been, for God will call to account what has passed.
Whatever exists was named long ago, and it is known what man is; but he cannot contend with one stronger than he.
Then I saw a new heaven and a new earth, for the first heaven and earth had passed away, and the sea was no more.
Then I turned to consider wisdom and madness and folly; for what more can the king’s successor do than what has already been accomplished?
Do not say, “Why were the old days better than these?” For it is unwise of you to ask about this.

verses.text: Is there a case where one can say, “Look, this is new”? It has already existed in the ages before us.

xrefs.text: You stiff-necked people with uncircumcised hearts and ears! You always resist the Holy Spirit, just as your fathers did.
Just as it was in the days of Noah, so also will it be in the days of the Son of Man:
And you say, ‘If we had lived in the days of our fathers, we would not have been partners with them in shedding the blood of the prophets.
Just as Jannes and Jambres opposed Moses, so also these men oppose the truth. They are depraved in mind and disqualified from the faith.
Rejoice and be glad, because great is your reward in heaven, for in the same way they persecuted the prophets before you.

verses.text: There is no remembrance of those who came before, and those yet to come will not be remembered by those who follow after.

xrefs.text: For there is no lasting remembrance of the wise, just as with the fool, seeing that both will be forgotten in the days to come. Alas, the wise man will die just like the fool!
The enemy has come to eternal ruin, and You have uprooted their cities; the very memory of them has vanished.
For the living know that they will die, but the dead know nothing. They have no further reward, because the memory of them is forgotten.
Behold, the former things have happened, and now I declare new things. Before they spring forth I proclaim them to you.”
“Let them come and tell us what will happen. Tell the former things, so that we may reflect on them and know the outcome. Or announce to us what is coming.

verses.text: I, the Teacher, was king over Israel in Jerusalem.

xrefs.text: These are the words of the Teacher, the son of David, king in Jerusalem:
So King Solomon ruled over Israel,

verses.text: And I set my mind to seek and explore by wisdom all that is done under heaven. What a miserable task God has laid upon the sons of men to occupy them!

xrefs.text: I have seen the burden that God has laid upon the sons of men to occupy them.
By the sweat of your brow you will eat your bread, until you return to the ground— because out of it were you taken. For dust you are, and to dust you shall return.”
When I applied my mind to know wisdom and to observe the task that one performs on the earth— though his eyes do not see sleep in the day or even in the night—
Be diligent in these matters and absorbed in them, so that your progress will be evident to all.
So I set my mind to know wisdom and madness and folly; I learned that this, too, is a pursuit of the wind.

verses.text: I have seen all the things that are done under the sun, and have found them all to be futile, a pursuit of the wind.

xrefs.text: Yet when I considered all the works that my hands had accomplished and what I had toiled to achieve, I found everything to be futile, a pursuit of the wind; there was nothing to be gained under the sun.
So I hated life, because the work that is done under the sun was grievous to me. For everything is futile and a pursuit of the wind.

To the man who is pleasing in His sight, He gives wisdom and knowledge and joy, but to the sinner He assigns the task of gathering and accumulating that which he will hand over to one who pleases God. This too is futile and a pursuit of the wind.
Better what the eye can see than the wandering of desire. This too is futile and a pursuit of the wind.
So I set my mind to know wisdom and madness and folly; I learned that this, too, is a pursuit of the wind.

verses.text: What is crooked cannot be straightened, and what is lacking cannot be counted.

xrefs.text: For wisdom, like money, is a shelter, and the advantage of knowledge is that wisdom preserves the life of its owner.
Who of you by worrying can add a single hour to his life?
I know that everything God does endures forever; nothing can be added to it or taken from it. God does it so that they should fear Him.
Every valley shall be lifted up, and every mountain and hill made low; the uneven ground will become smooth, and the rugged land a plain.
and disclose to you the secrets of wisdom, for true wisdom has two sides. Know then that God exacts from you less than your iniquity deserves.

verses.text: I said to myself, “Behold, I have grown and increased in wisdom beyond all those before me who were over Jerusalem, and my mind has observed a wealth of wisdom and knowledge.”

xrefs.text: So I became great and surpassed all in Jerusalem who had preceded me; and my wisdom remained with me.
Solomon’s wisdom was greater than that of all the men of the East, greater than all the wisdom of Egypt.
But I did not believe these things until I came and saw with my own eyes. Indeed, not even half was told to me. Your wisdom and prosperity have far exceeded the report I heard.
Be angry, yet do not sin; on your bed, search your heart and be still. Selah

verses.text: So I set my mind to know wisdom and madness and folly; I learned that this, too, is a pursuit of the wind.

xrefs.text: I sought to cheer my body with wine and to embrace folly— my mind still guiding me with wisdom— until I could see what was worthwhile for men to do under heaven during the few days of their lives.

And I set my mind to seek and explore by wisdom all that is done under heaven. What a miserable task God has laid upon the sons of men to occupy them!
All this I tested by wisdom, saying, “I resolve to be wise.” But it was beyond me.
Anything my eyes desired, I did not deny myself. I refused my heart no pleasure. For my heart took delight in all my work, and this was the reward for all my labor.

verses.text: For with much wisdom comes much sorrow, and as knowledge grows, grief increases.

xrefs.text: And He said to man, ‘Behold, the fear of the Lord, that is wisdom, and to turn away from evil is understanding.’”
And by these, my son, be further warned: There is no end to the making of many books, and much study wearies the body.
Let no one deceive himself. If any of you thinks he is wise in this age, he should become a fool, so that he may become wise.
Do not be overly righteous, and do not make yourself too wise. Why should you destroy yourself?
Indeed, all his days are filled with grief, and his task is sorrowful; even at night, his mind does not rest. This too is futile.
